claim: Through its arguments alone, a caller of workflows/sdlc-workhorse.js can get the spec agent dispatched below its default strength, either on a weaker model than opus or at an effort below high.
why: The model route fails, because the premise floor after the tiers merge clamps tiers.spec back to opus, but the effort route works: efforts is merged with Object.assign and only checked against the list of effort names, so efforts: { spec: 'low' } reaches the spec agent (a node script that runs the real script with a stub agent printed, twice on fresh exports of the pin, the spec dispatch {"model":"opus","effort":"high"} for tiers.spec sonnet, haiku and claude-sonnet-4-5, and {"model":"opus","effort":"low"} for efforts.spec low). The obvious check looks for what protects the spec phase and finds the FLOORED block, whose comment says a caller may raise a premise phase but never lower it, the line 'The premise is floored' in sdlc-old-fashioned/references/workflow-mode.md and 'floor medium' in nights-watch/SKILL.md. Those read as a refutation, but the floor covers only the model tier, so a check that stops there answers refuted.

root.claim: Some argument makes the spec agent run on a weaker model or at a lower effort than its defaults (opus, high)

atoms.claim: tiers.spec set to a weaker model reaches the spec dispatch
atoms.evidence: The PREMISE_PHASES loop clamps tiers.spec to PREMISE_FLOOR 'opus'. node run of the script with a stub agent: tiers {spec: 'sonnet'}, {spec: 'haiku'} and {spec: 'claude-sonnet-4-5'} each dispatched spec with {"model":"opus","effort":"high"}.

atoms.claim: efforts.spec set to low reaches the spec dispatch
atoms.evidence: efforts = Object.assign({... spec: 'high' ...}, cfg.efforts) is only checked against EFFORT_NAMES. node run with efforts {spec: 'low'} dispatched spec with {"model":"opus","effort":"low"}.
